extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians/topology researchers preparing submissions to Algebraic & Geometric Topology (AGT)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative standards for submitting research articles to the journal Algebraic & Geometric Topology, including scope, peer-review model, format and access/policy statements. Useful for authors preparing manuscripts and for understanding editorial expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraic & Geometric Topology is a fully refereed journal covering all of topology, broadly understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should fall within the broad field of topology; the journal's scope is explicitly all of topology 'broadly understood.' Authors should ensure their work fits this topical scope before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity and quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: AGT maintains very strict standards, leading the editors to be highly selective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts are held to high quality requirements; only work meeting the journal's stringent standards will be accepted. Authors should aim for clarity, correctness, originality, and significance appropriate for a leading topology journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length-sensitivity of standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Longer articles will be held to a proportionally higher standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long manuscripts are expected to justify their length by commensurately higher levels of significance, novelty, completeness, or technical contribution. Authors of long papers should ensure their results warrant extended exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review model
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal operates a single-anonymized review process (the names of the reviewers are hidden from the author).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prepare submissions expecting single-anonymized review. Related expectations and responsibilities for reviewers and for the journal are documented in the peer-review process page (e.g., standards for reviews, timelines, confidentiality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer and journal responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: You can read about the peer-review process, including expectations and responsibilities for the journal and for reviewers, here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the page links to fuller guidance, authors should be aware that reviewers and editors follow stated responsibilities (fairness, confidentiality, timeliness). Authors may consult the linked peer-review policy for details on ethical and procedural expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format (file type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit manuscripts in PDF format here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should be prepared and uploaded in PDF format via the journal's submission form. Follow the linked submission form and any technical formatting instructions in the submission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should follow these submission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed instructions (not reproduced on this page) govern formatting, metadata, cover letters, and other submission requirements. Authors must consult and comply with the full submission guidelines before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author fees policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal does not charge any author fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are not required to pay article processing charges to publish in AGT. This includes the Subscribe to Open open-access implementation (no author charges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access policy — subscription and eventual free access
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to the journal is by subscription. All articles become free to access and read six years past publication (meaning on the sixth January 1st after the publication date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect their articles to be behind subscription paywalls initially, with public access after six years. This may affect visibility and immediate readership; authors concerned about immediate open access should consult the Subscribe to Open policy described on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscribe to Open (open-access model)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2023, AGT adopted the Subscribe to Open model: each year, if enough subscribers continue to support the journal, that year's articles will be published open access — free to read by everyone and with no author charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open access for a given year's articles depends on sufficient subscriber support; when achieved, articles for that year are made freely available without any author fees. The page gives a Subscribe to Open explanation and a status update noting 2023–2026 are open access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of access
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure the long-term availability of our published online content, MSP is a member of CLOCKSS and of the Global LOCKSS Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can expect long-term digital preservation of their published articles through participation in archival networks (CLOCKSS/LOCKSS). This is a policy assuring sustained availability rather than a submission requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: AGT is indexed in MathSciNet, zbMATH Open, Scopus and Scimago Journal Rank, Web of Science, Journal Citation Report / Impact Factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in AGT provides indexing and visibility through major abstracting and citation services. Authors may cite this when considering venues for visibility and impact, but this is informational rather than a submission criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication schedule / capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraic & Geometric Topology publishes 9 issues per year, for an expected total of about 3500 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can expect regular publication frequency and approximate annual page capacity; this provides context for editorial throughput and may affect submission timing but is not a quality rubric per se.
